unit.label: Transportation, companions & implicit comparison
unit.title: How Are You Getting There?
unit.description: 12 new words and forms. Start this lesson with transportation, going with someone, asking how, implicit comparison with 比較, and 又…又….

goal.meaning: How do you go to school?

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 8, pp. 160–174. Transportation vocabulary and grammar I–IV; explicit 比 is intentionally left for the next unit. Original Hanzi Steps examples and exercises.

steps.prompt: Which phrase means “take the train”?
steps.explanation: Use 坐 before the vehicle.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 坐 is zuò; before transport it means take/travel by.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 車 is chē, vehicle.

lessons.title: Go with a Friend
lessons.subtitle: Use 跟 for companionship and 玩 as an action.

steps.prompt: Who accompanies the speaker in 我跟朋友去玩?
steps.explanation: 跟 introduces the companion.

steps.prompt: Which is the standalone action “to play; have fun”?
steps.explanation: 玩 is the action verb; 好玩 describes something as fun.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 跟 is gēn: with; follow.

lessons.title: How Do You Go?
lessons.subtitle: Ask about the method of an action and keep 怎麼 distinct from 怎麼樣.

steps.prompt: You want to know the method of getting to school. Which question fits?
steps.explanation: 怎麼 comes before the action phrase to ask how it is done.

steps.prompt: You want an evaluation of the train. Which question fits?
steps.explanation: 怎麼樣 asks how something is or what someone thinks of it.

lessons.title: Faster or Slower
lessons.subtitle: Use 比較 when the comparison is understood from context.

steps.prompt: In Taiwan usage taught here, what does 比較 signal?
steps.explanation: 比較 says something is comparatively/more so, with the comparison understood from context.

steps.prompt: Which word means “fast”?
steps.explanation: 快 means fast; 慢 means slow.

steps.prompt: You are less busy lately than before. Which matches?
steps.explanation: The negative belongs to 忙: 比較 + 不忙. 比較忙 would mean busier.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 慢 is màn: slow.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 快 is kuài: fast; quick.

lessons.title: High Speed Rail & Tickets
lessons.subtitle: Learn 高鐵 and 車票, then use the comparison you just learned.

steps.prompt: Which word means “High Speed Rail”?
steps.explanation: 高鐵 is the common abbreviation for High Speed Rail.

steps.prompt: Which word means “ticket” in this lesson?
steps.explanation: 車票 is a transportation ticket.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 鐵 is tiě, the second character of 高鐵.

lessons.title: Both Fast and Comfortable
lessons.subtitle: Join two properties with 又…又….

steps.prompt: What two properties are linked in 高鐵又快又舒服?
steps.explanation: The two 又 markers coordinate 快 and 舒服.

steps.prompt: Complete the pattern: 又快___舒服
steps.explanation: Repeat 又 before the second coordinated property.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 又 is yòu; the repeated pair forms 又…又….

steps.prompt: Both qualities are negative. Complete: 這支手機又不好看___不好玩。
steps.explanation: Repeat 又 before the second negative predicate as well.

steps.prompt: 我又想喝茶又想喝咖啡 expresses which wishes?
steps.explanation: 又 repeats before 想喝茶 and 想喝咖啡; both wishes hold.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 舒 is shū: comfortable; relaxed.

lessons.title: Unit 24 Review
lessons.subtitle: Transportation, companions, method questions, and implicit comparison.

steps.prompt: Which asks how an action is done?
steps.explanation: 怎麼 asks for the method of 去學校.

steps.prompt: Which says High Speed Rail is relatively faster?
steps.explanation: 比較 marks the implicit comparison.

steps.prompt: Which says the speaker has been LESS busy lately?
steps.explanation: 比較不忙 compares the lower degree of busyness with an understood earlier situation.

steps.prompt: Which says the phone is NEITHER good-looking NOR fun?
options: 這支手機又不好看又不好玩。
這支手機又好看又好玩。
這支手機又不好看又好玩。
steps.answer: 這支手機又不好看又不好玩。
steps.explanation: Each property needs its own negative: 又不…又不….

steps.prompt: 我跟朋友坐火車 tells you what?
options: The ticket price and departure time
steps.explanation: 跟朋友 names the companion; 坐火車 names the transport.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 跟 is gēn: with; follow.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 慢 is màn: slow.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 較 is jiào: compare; relatively.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 舒 is shū: comfortable; relaxed.

steps.prompt: You want an opinion about the train, not instructions for travelling. Which question fits?
steps.explanation: 怎麼樣 requests an evaluation; 怎麼 before an action asks about its method.

newVocabulary.note: In the Taiwan usage taught here, 比較 signals a comparison even when the standard is understood from context.

坐.note: 坐 is fourth-tone zuò. Before a vehicle, it means to take or travel by that vehicle.
坐.memory: Two 人-like figures sit above 土. Keep the final three 土 strokes centered under the four upper strokes.

parts.label: 从
parts.name: two-person upper group
parts.description: The first four strokes form the paired person-like upper group.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 土 underneath.

火.note: 火 is third-tone huǒ. In 火車 it is the first character of the word for train.
火.memory: Two small side strokes frame the central 人-like pair, making a four-stroke flame shape.

parts.label: side
parts.name: side strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes are the shorter side strokes of the flame.

parts.label: 人
parts.name: central pair
parts.description: The final two strokes spread downward through the center like 人.

車.note: 車 is first-tone chē. It appears in 火車 'train' and 車票 'ticket'.
車.memory: A central vertical passes through a boxed middle and three horizontal levels. Keep the seven strokes balanced around the center.

parts.label: 車
parts.name: whole vehicle form
parts.description: Write the seven-stroke traditional 車 as a single centered framework with the long vertical crossing its horizontal levels.

跟.note: 跟 is first-tone gēn. In this lesson it introduces the person who accompanies someone in an activity.
跟.memory: The seven-stroke 足 component stands on the left; 艮 fills the six-stroke right side.

parts.label: 𧾷
parts.name: foot component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form the compressed foot component on the left.

parts.label: 艮
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 艮 on the right.

慢.note: 慢 is fourth-tone màn. It describes something as slow, including a mode of transportation.
慢.memory: The three-stroke 忄 heart side stays narrow; the eleven-stroke 曼 block fills the right.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: heart side
parts.description: The first three strokes form 忄 on the left.

parts.label: 曼
parts.name: right block
parts.description: The final eleven strokes form the larger 曼 component on the right.

較.note: 較 is fourth-tone jiào. Together with 比 it forms 比較, the adverb used for an implicit comparison.
較.memory: Traditional 車 takes the first seven strokes; 交 supplies the six-stroke right side.

parts.label: 車
parts.name: vehicle component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 車 on the left.

parts.label: 交
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 交 on the right.

快.note: 快 is fourth-tone kuài. It contrasts with 慢 when comparing transportation.
快.memory: Three-stroke 忄 on the left is followed by four-stroke 夬 on the right.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: heart side
parts.description: The first three strokes form the narrow 忄 component.

parts.label: 夬
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 夬 on the right, ending in the spreading lower stroke.

高.note: 高 is first-tone gāo. In 高鐵 it is part of Taiwan's common abbreviation for High Speed Rail.
高.memory: A two-stroke 亠 sits above a small 口, then the five-stroke lower enclosure completes 高.

parts.label: 亠
parts.name: top
parts.description: The first two strokes form the cap at the top.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: middle mouth
parts.description: The next three strokes form the small central 口.

parts.label: 冋
parts.name: lower frame
parts.description: The final five strokes form the broad lower enclosure.

鐵.note: 鐵 is third-tone tiě. In 高鐵 it refers to the rail part of High Speed Rail.
鐵.memory: 金 uses the first eight strokes on the left; the dense thirteen-stroke 𢧜 fills the right.

parts.label: 金
parts.name: metal component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the metal radical 金 on the left.

parts.label: 𢧜
parts.name: right block
parts.description: The final thirteen strokes form the compact right-side component.

票.note: 票 is fourth-tone piào. 車票 means a ticket for transportation.
票.memory: Six-stroke 覀 forms the top; five-stroke 示 forms the lower half.

parts.label: 覀
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 覀 across the top.

parts.label: 示
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 示 below.

又.note: 又 is fourth-tone yòu. Repeated as 又…又…, it links two properties: both A and B.
又.memory: 又 is only two crossing strokes: a bent first stroke followed by a long falling-right stroke.

parts.label: 又
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: The two strokes cross to form the complete character; keep the second stroke long and open.

舒.note: 舒 is first-tone shū. It is the first character of 舒服, 'comfortable'.
舒.memory: 舍 fills the first eight strokes on the left and 予 uses the final four strokes on the right.

parts.label: 舍
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 舍 on the left.

parts.label: 予
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 予 on the right.

服.note: 服 is read with a neutral tone in the common word 舒服: shūfu. The character's citation reading is fú.
服.memory: 月 forms the four-stroke left side; the final four strokes form 𠬝 on the right.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 月 on the left.

parts.label: 𠬝
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final four strokes form the right-hand component.

u24-zuo-transport.title: Take transportation with 坐
u24-zuo-transport.explanation: Before a mode of transportation, 坐 means to take or travel by that vehicle. The vehicle follows 坐 directly; a destination can follow 去.

examples.meaning: I take the train to school.
I go by High Speed Rail.

u24-zuo-transport.remember: 坐 + vehicle tells how you travel.

u24-gen-company.title: Companionship with 跟
u24-gen-company.explanation: 跟 introduces the person who accompanies the subject in an activity. Put 跟 + person before the action phrase.

examples.meaning: I go have fun with a friend.
I take the train with a friend.

u24-gen-company.remember: 跟 + person comes before the shared activity.

u24-how-zenme.title: Ask how with 怎麼
u24-how-zenme.explanation: 怎麼 is a question adverb used to ask how an action is done. Put it before the action verb or action phrase.

examples.meaning: How do you go to school?

u24-how-zenme.remember: If the answer would describe a method, use 怎麼 before the action.

u24-how-vs-zenmeyang.title: 怎麼 is not 怎麼樣
u24-how-vs-zenmeyang.pattern: 怎麼 + Action? vs. Topic + 怎麼樣?
u24-how-vs-zenmeyang.explanation: 怎麼 asks how an action is carried out. 怎麼樣 is a state-verb expression asking how something is or what someone thinks about it. They are not interchangeable.

examples.meaning: How do you go to school?
How is the train? / What do you think of the train?

u24-how-vs-zenmeyang.remember: Method of an action → 怎麼. Evaluation of a topic → 怎麼樣.

u24-bijiao.title: Implicit comparison with 比較
u24-bijiao.explanation: 比較 marks an implicit comparison: the comparison standard is understood from context. In the Taiwan usage taught here, 比較 retains this comparative meaning. If the description is negated, put the negative with the main description, as in 比較不貴, rather than negating 比較 itself.

examples.meaning: High Speed Rail is relatively faster.
I have been less busy lately.

u24-bijiao.remember: 比較 tells the listener to compare with something understood from context.

u24-you-you.title: Both A and B with 又…又…
u24-you-you.pattern: 又 + Property A + 又 + Property B
u24-you-you.explanation: Use 又 before each of two coordinated properties to say that something has both qualities. The two descriptions apply to the same topic. The pattern can also be used with wishes or abilities, not only simple adjectives. To make both descriptions negative, place 不 after each 又: 又不…又不….

examples.meaning: High Speed Rail is both fast and comfortable.

examples.text: 這支手機又好看又好玩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī shǒujī yòu hǎokàn yòu hǎowán.
examples.meaning: This phone is both good-looking and fun.

examples.text: 這支手機又不好看又不好玩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī shǒujī yòu bù hǎokàn yòu bù hǎowán.
examples.meaning: This phone is neither good-looking nor fun.

examples.text: 我又想喝茶又想喝咖啡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yòu xiǎng hē chá yòu xiǎng hē kāfēi.
examples.meaning: I want both tea and coffee.

u24-you-you.remember: Repeat 又 before both predicates; put 不 after each 又 when both are negative.

u24-train-school.meaning: I take the train to school.
u24-train-school.note: 坐 + vehicle gives the mode of transportation.

u24-friend-play.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò gēn péngyǒu qù wán.
u24-friend-play.meaning: I go have fun with a friend on the weekend.
u24-friend-play.note: 跟朋友 precedes the shared action.

u24-how-school.meaning: How do you go to school?
u24-how-school.note: 怎麼 asks for the method of 去學校.

u24-train-opinion.meaning: How is the train? / What do you think of the train?
u24-train-opinion.note: 怎麼樣 asks for an evaluation, not a method.

u24-train-slower.note: The comparison standard is supplied by context.

u24-hsr-faster.meaning: High Speed Rail is relatively faster.
u24-hsr-faster.note: 比較 marks an implicit comparison.

u24-ticket-price.meaning: High Speed Rail tickets are a little expensive.
u24-ticket-price.note: 有一點 softens a negative-ish description such as 貴.

u24-fast-comfortable.meaning: High Speed Rail is both fast and comfortable.
u24-fast-comfortable.note: 又 is repeated before each property.

u24-less-busy.meaning: I have been less busy lately.
u24-less-busy.note: The comparison is with the earlier situation. 比較 stays before the negative description 不忙.

u24-phone-neither.text: 這支手機又不好看又不好玩。
u24-phone-neither.pinyin: Zhè zhī shǒujī yòu bù hǎokàn yòu bù hǎowán.
u24-phone-neither.meaning: This phone is neither good-looking nor fun.
u24-phone-neither.note: Both descriptions are negative: repeat 又不 before each one.
